<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par47 />stem-form was not always sufficient to express at the same time differences both of gender and number, the distinction had to be further indicated, in several cases, by special ''afformatives''. Cf. the table, {{GHGpar|40|c}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|b}}
'''2.''' The derivation and meaning, both of the preformatives and the afformatives, can still, in most cases, be recognized.

In the ''first'' pers. {{GHGheb|text=אֶקְטֹל}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=נִקְטֹל}}, {{GHGheb|text=א}} is probably connected with {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}}, and {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}} with {{GHGheb|text=נָ֫חְנוּ}}; here no indication of gender or number by a special ending was necessary. As regards the vocalization, the Arabic points to the ground-forms ''ʾăqṭŭl'' and ''năqṭŭl'': the ''ĭ'' of the 1st plur. is, therefore, as in the other preformatives, attenuated from ''a''. The {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} of the 1st sing. is probably to be explained by the preference of the {{GHGheb|text=א}} for this sound (cf. {{GHGpar|22|o}}, but also {{GHGpar|51|p}}); according to Qimḥi, it arises from an endeavour to avoid the similarity of sound between {{GHGheb|text=אִקְטֹל}} (which is the Babylonian punctuation) and {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטֹל}}, which, according to this view, was likewise pronounced ''iqṭōl''.<ref>Cf. {{GHGpar|24|e}}. In favour of the above view of Qimḥi may be urged the phonetic orthography {{GHGheb|text=אִשׁ}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=18|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=19}} (unless, with Perles, {{GHGheb|text=אָשֻׁב}} is to be read), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=10}}, for {{GHGheb|text=יֵשׁ}}, and {{GHGheb|text=אִישַׁי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=2|verse=13}} for {{GHGheb|text=יִשַׁי}} (as verse 12). Also {{GHGheb|text=הַֽאֶזְכֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=11}} is probably for {{GHGheb|text=הַֽאִזְ׳}} = {{GHGheb|text=הֲיִזְ׳}}, {{GHGheb|text=אפקד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=12}} for {{GHGheb|text=יִפְקֹד}}; {{GHGheb|text=אנחמך}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=19}} for {{GHGheb|text=יְנַֽחֲמֵךְ}}; and conversely {{GHGheb|text=יששכר}} is for {{GHGheb|text=אשש׳}}={{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ שָׂכָר}}. Similarly, {{GHGheb|text=ישוי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=49}} is probably for {{GHGheb|text=אִשְׁיוֹ}} or {{GHGheb|text=אִשְׁיָה}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=ישׁב בשבת}} is, according to the LXX, an error for {{GHGheb|text=ישבשת}}={{GHGheb|text=אִשְׁבּ֫שֶׁת}}. In Assyrian also the simple ''i'' corresponds to the Hebrew {{GHGheb|text=י}} as the preformative of the Impf. Qal.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|c}}
The preformative {{GHGheb|text=ת}} of the ''second'' persons ({{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹל}}, ground-form ''tăqṭŭl'', &c.) is, without doubt, connected with the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} of {{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַתֶּם}}. &c., and the ''afformative'' {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} of the 2nd fem. sing. {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטְלִי}} with the ''i'' of the original feminine form {{GHGheb|text=אַתִּי}} (see {{GHGpar|32|h}}). The ''afformative'' {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} of the 2nd masc. plur. {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטְלוּ}} (in its more complete form, {{GHGheb|text=וּן}}, see m) is the sign of the plural, as in the 3rd pers., and also in the Perfect ({{GHGpar|44|a}}). In the Imperfect, however, it is restricted in both persons to the masculine,<ref>This is also the proper gender of the plural syllable ''û'', ''ûn''. In Hebrew, indeed, it is used in the 3rd plur. {{GHGterm|Perfect}} for both genders, but in the kindred languages even there only for the masculine, e.g. in Syriac ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭálû, q<sup>e</sup>ṭálûn'', with the feminine form ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭálên'', in Western Aram. ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭálû'', fem. ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭálā''; in Arab. ''qătălû'', fem. ''qătálnă'', Eth. ''qătălû'', ''qătălâ''.</ref> while the afformative {{GHGheb|text=נָה}} (also {{GHGheb|text=ןָ}}) of the 3rd and 2nd plur. fem. is probably connected with {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫נָּה|translate=eae}} and {{GHGheb|text=אַתֵּ֫נָה|translate=vos}} (fem.).

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|d}}
The preformatives of the ''third'' persons ({{GHGheb|text=י}} in the masc. {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטֹל}}, ground-form ''yăqṭŭl'', plur. {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטְלוּ}}, ground-form ''yăqṭŭlû''; {{GHGheb|text=ת}} in the fem. {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹל}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹ֫לְנָה}}) have not yet met with any satisfactory explanation. With {{GHGheb|text=ת}} might most obviously be compared the original feminine<section end=par47 /><noinclude>
